See also: pilóta, pilotá, and pilotă

Basque

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Spanish pelota.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): (Navarro-Lapurdian) /pilota/ [pi.lo.t̪a]
  • IPA(key): (Southern) /piʎota/ [pi.ʎo.t̪a]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -ota, -a
  • Hyphenation: pi‧lo‧ta

Noun

[edit]

pilota inan

  1. Basque pelota

Derived terms

[edit]
  • pilotaleku
  • pilotari

Catalan

[edit]

Etymology 1

[edit]

From Vulgar Latin *pilotta, diminutive of pila. Compare French pelote, Spanish pelota.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): (Central, Balearic) [piˈlɔ.tə]
  • IPA(key): (Valencia) [piˈlɔ.ta]
  • Audio:(file)

Noun

[edit]

pilota f (plural pilotes)

  1. ball
    Synonym: baló
  2. (vulgar) bollock, testicle
  3. a musket ball
  4. a large meatball
Derived terms
[edit]
  • esport de pilota
  • la pilota és a la teulada d'algú
  • passar la pilota
  • pilota basca
  • pilotada
  • pilotaire
  • pilotejar
  • piloter
Related terms
[edit]
  • pilotari
  • pilotilla

Further reading

[edit]
  • “pilota” in Diccionari català-valencià-balear, Antoni Maria Alcover and Francesc de Borja Moll, 1962.
  • “pilota”, in Gran Diccionari de la Llengua Catalana, Grup Enciclopèdia Catalana, 2026

Etymology 2

[edit]

Verb

[edit]

pilota

  1. inflection of pilotar:
    1. third-person singular present indicative
    2. second-person singular imperative

[edit]

Pronunciation

Verb

pilota

  1. third-person singular past historic of piloter

Italian

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /piˈlɔ.ta/
  • Rhymes: -ɔta
  • Hyphenation: pi‧lò‧ta

Etymology 1

[edit]

From earlier pedota, pedotta, from Byzantine Greek *πηδώτης (*pēdṓtēs, “helmsman”), from Ancient Greek πηδόν (pēdón, “oarblade, oar”). The pil- forms are probably influenced by pileggiare (“to sail, navigate”).

Noun

[edit]

pilota m or f by sense (masculine plural piloti, feminine plural pilote)

  1. pilot (aircraft or ship)
  2. driver (vehicle)
Descendants
[edit]

Including descendants from piloto m.

  • → Catalan: pilot
  • → Greek: πιλότος (pilótos)
  • → Middle French: pilot, pillot
    • French: pilote (see there for further descendants)
    • → Dutch: piloot
      • → Papiamentu: pilot
    • → English: pilot (see there for further descendants)
  • → Portuguese: piloto
  • → Spanish: piloto
    • → Tagalog: piloto

Adjective

[edit]

pilota (invariable)

  1. (relational) pilot

Etymology 2

[edit]

See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

Verb

[edit]

pilota

  1. inflection of pilotare:
    1. third-person singular present indicative
    2. second-person singular imperative

Anagrams

[edit]
  • Pilato, oplita, polita

Latvian

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

pilota

  1. genitive singular of pilots

Polish

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /piˈlɔ.ta/
  • Rhymes: -ɔta
  • Syllabification: pi‧lo‧ta

Noun

[edit]

pilota m

  1. genitive singular of pilot
  2. accusative singular of pilot (in the meaning of: aircraft pilot)
  3. (colloquial) accusative singular of pilot (in the meaning of: remote control)

Portuguese

[edit]

Etymology 1

[edit]

From pilar +‎ -ota.

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /piˈlɔ.tɐ/
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /piˈlɔ.tɐ/
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /piˈlɔ.ta/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /piˈlɔ.tɐ/

  • Rhymes: -ɔtɐ

Noun

[edit]

pilota f (plural pilotas)

  1. exhaustion
  2. (finance) loss
  3. defeat
  4. castigation, reprimand
